newsitem.title: USA: Arraignment of former ADM executives postponed.
newsitem.headline: Arraignment of former ADM executives postponed.

text.p: The arraignment of three former Archer Daniels Midland Co executives facing price-fixing charges was postponed Monday after U.S. prosecutors failed to get the case assigned to a different judge.

First Assistant U.S. Attorney Scott Lassar said U.S. District Judge Blanche Manning will preside over the case against Michael Andreas, who recently took leave as vice chairman of ADM; Terrance Wilson, a former group vice president in charge of corn refining; and Mark Whitacre, who had headed ADM's BioProducts Division.
The three were charged with allegedly fixing prices of lysine, a feed additive.
The case was assigned originally to Manning, but U.S. prosecutors had attempted to have it transferred to Judge Ruben Castillo.

Castillo presided over ADM's antitrust case, in which the company pleaded guilty to two counts of fixing prices of lysine and citric acid, a food and feed additive. ADM also agreed to pay a record $100 million in fines.
As of Monday morning, no date had been set for the arraignments.
